source.title: Scaling Law for Quantization-Aware Training
source.authors: Meng-Zhao Chen; Chaoyi Zhang; Jing Liu; Yutao Zeng; Ze-Yue Xue; Zhi-Heng Liu; Yunshui Li; Jin Ma; Jie Huang; Xun Zhou; Ping Luo

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The appendix fits a Chinchilla-style loss scaling law to OLMo2 model losses using the stated original-style fitting procedure; the paper also tests a QAT quantization-error scaling law and larger-model predictions.
record.gate_note: The main experiments measure the loss gap between QAT and BF16 models (quantization error), not the ordinary held-out pretraining loss named by most claim versions. The appendix separately reports a Chinchilla loss-law fit. Results about weight/activation decomposition, kurtosis and mixed precision are not separate evidence for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The main contribution is a scaling law for the QAT quantization-error gap, which is a different construct from pretraining loss. Only Appendix C bears on a version. It fits the Chinchilla loss law L(N,D) to BF16 OLMo2-style models from 145M to 12.7B with Chinchilla's own procedure (Huber loss on log loss, L-BFGS) and reports fit quality, which bears on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that 4-bit QAT quantization error is best modelled jointly by model size, training tokens and granularity, and that this predicts more accurately than prior N-only laws. They also conclude that an 8-bit FC2 input cuts error and granularity sensitivity. After that fix, weight and activation errors contribute about equally, so future QAT work should also target weight error.
record.recipe_differences: The appendix uses a Chinchilla-style loss law and original-style fitting procedure; the main contribution instead fits a new law for QAT quantization error that adds training-token count and quantization granularity.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported results and fitted exponents vary with quantization precision, granularity, training-token count and whether the FC2 input is quantized to 8-bit.

fits_no_version.finding: The QAT quantization-error gap follows k·D^γD·(log2 G)^γG/N^γN. The exponents differ by precision (W4A4, W4A16, W16A4, FC2 at 8-bit). Including D and G cuts relative error from 8.5–19.3% to 4.7–5.2%. The fit extrapolates to 973M models at 100B and 200B tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The low-bit QAT loss gap versus BF16 scales as a power law, decreasing in model size and increasing in training tokens and group size.

fits_no_version.finding: W4A4 error falls 34% from 74M to 594M, rises 22% from 10B to 100B tokens, and is smaller with finer granularity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization error in QAT grows with the data-to-parameter ratio.

record.problems: The study primarily measures QAT quantization-error gaps rather than ordinary held-out loss. It uses smoothed training loss as an estimate of validation loss. Larger-run QAT validation is described as consistently accurate without separate numerical errors for the 973M conditions. The largest QAT experiment is reported as a 595M model trained over 100B tokens; the authors note that larger experiments could improve extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed weight-versus-activation decomposition, kurtosis, FC2 outlier analysis and mixed-precision effects are omitted because they do not directly measure a listed claim version. Appendix C's individual model loss points are not separately tabulated in the text.

untested.parts: Scaling in compute. Each axis alone with the others non-bottlenecking. Held-out loss (training loss is used). Fitted exponents for α and β separately (α=β is imposed).
Not tested for pretraining loss; the Chinchilla fit is in-sample only.
Not tested. The QAT results model a loss gap, not loss under a new regime.
Not tested for loss laws. α=β is assumed, not compared with a free fit.

missing.what: Fitted Chinchilla constants for BF16 loss: E=1.9279, A=237.70, B=596.25, α=β=0.3022 (α=β imposed).

record.verdict_notes: The only link to the claim is the Appendix C Chinchilla fit. It is a supporting baseline for the paper's QAT work, not a stress test of V1. The record's V2 and V7 links were to the quantization-error law, a different construct, and have been removed.

versions.untested_parts: The appendix fits loss against model size and training data, but does not independently test each resource axis with the other two non-bottlenecking, or test loss scaling directly against training compute.
The larger-run validation is for the paper's QAT quantization-error law; it does not establish general extrapolation of ordinary pretraining loss from small runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or measurement of the loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation is reported.
There is no controlled comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns text-model QAT and does not test other modalities, fine-tuning or transfer.

The study compares QAT quantization settings and model forms, but does not test compute-optimal allocations, parameter-counting choices, training-schedule choices, or systematic changes to the fitting method.

rows.subject: OLMo2 models (145M to 12.7B parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Fit a Chinchilla loss scaling law to empirical losses, with α = β.

conditions.value: OLMo2-Mix-1124; training-data sizes not stated for every model
Huber loss between predicted and observed log losses; L-BFGS

rows.note: The text says empirical training losses closely match predicted losses. The losses are used as an estimate of validation loss elsewhere in the paper.
rows.check: Value is right (MSE 0.0014, R2 0.982; the figure gives 0.001472). The fit imposes α=β=0.3022 rather than estimating it. The 6.5B and 12.7B points are official OLMo2 releases trained differently from the authors' runs. The loss is smoothed training loss, not held-out loss. This is an in-sample fit, not an extrapolation test. Per-model token counts are not stated.

relationships.condition: BF16 Llama3/OLMo2-style models, 145M–12.7B, OLMo2-Mix data, Chinchilla form with α=β
relationships.reason: A Chinchilla power-law fit matches the observed losses closely (R2 0.982, MSE 0.0014) over about two orders of magnitude in N (r1). The evidence is weak: an in-sample fit with a constrained exponent.
relationships.display_finding: The constrained Chinchilla power-law fit achieved R² of 0.982 and mean squared error of 0.0014 across about two orders of magnitude in parameters.
